title: Case study: distributed key-value store
summary: Dynamo-style store derived from the requirements: ops-sized estimation, hash ring and preference lists, tunable quorums with sloppy quorums and hints, conflict resolution per data type, Merkle-tree repair and tombstones, gossip membership, and the flip to consensus.

units.title: Guided design: requirements, estimation, API and data model, from one node to a ring
Deep dives: quorums under failure, conflicts, anti-entropy and deletes, membership and the CP flip

labs.title: Merkle-tree anti-entropy: deterministic merge with tombstones, trees over token buckets, diff by descent, repair of only the divergent leaves, safe tombstone purge
Gossip membership: generation-aware heartbeats, suspect and dead states, dead-member probing across partitions, phi-accrual failure detector

outcomes.text: Scope a distributed key-value store prompt in ≤ 6 minutes: core operations, NFRs with numbers, out-of-scope list, and the clarifying questions (consistency per operation, partition behaviour, concurrent-write semantics, scans, regions) whose answers pick between the leaderless and the consensus families.

Estimate storage with replication and LSM overhead, replica operations (reads × R + writes × N), nodes by operations vs by disk, replication and cross-AZ bandwidth, hint volume and rebuild time, and state the decision each drives.

Design the API (consistency level per request, opaque causal context, siblings, Unavailable vs Timeout, tombstone deletes) and the per-node data model (LSM sorted by token, versions, tombstones, TTL).

Build the high-level design step by step: hash ring with virtual nodes, preference lists over distinct nodes and AZs, any-node coordination with token-aware clients, read and write paths at QUORUM with rates, and the background processes each requirement forces.
Choose N, R, W and strict vs sloppy quorums per operation, explain what R + W > N does and does not guarantee, and size and bound hinted handoff.
Choose conflict resolution per data type (last-write-wins, version vectors with siblings, CRDTs such as PN-counters and OR-Sets, or prevention by consensus) and explain how each alternative fails.

Implement Merkle-tree anti-entropy that ships only the divergent leaves, deterministic merging with tombstones, and tombstone garbage collection with a safe cutoff, and demonstrate zombie resurrection (labs/c4/antientropy).
Explain gossip membership and failure detection (heartbeat generations, suspicion, phi accrual), why conviction reroutes while removal streams, how nodes join and leave, and how to handle hot keys.
Decide when the answer flips to consensus (per-key Paxos vs Raft groups per range vs a separate CP store) for compare-and-set, with latency and partition behaviour stated.

Implement gossip membership with generation-aware heartbeats, suspect and dead states, dead-member probing and a phi-accrual detector (labs/c4/membership), and reason about multi-region quorums (LOCAL_QUORUM vs EACH_QUORUM).
